Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. subtopics.name: Discharge planning and continuity of care

questions.stem: At 1600 the nurse on a surgical unit has four clients. Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A client 1 day after a laparoscopic cholecystectomy who reports right shoulder pain of 5 of 10 and has not passed gas
A client 3 hours after a carotid endarterectomy whose voice is hoarse and who has a new swelling on the side of the neck
A client 2 days after a total knee replacement whose continuous passive motion machine keeps stopping at 60 degrees of flexion
A client 4 hours after a transurethral resection of the prostate whose urine is light pink with small clots

rationale.correct: A possible airway threat after neck surgery comes before expected postoperative findings and equipment problems.

perOption.a: Shoulder pain from the gas used in laparoscopy and no flatus on day 1 are expected.
perOption.b: Neck swelling after carotid surgery can be a hematoma that compresses the airway; hoarseness suggests nerve or airway involvement.
perOption.c: Equipment problems need attention, but they do not threaten life.
perOption.d: Light pink urine with small clots is expected early after TURP.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Medical-surgical nursing texts (e.g. Lewis; Ignatavicius)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Prioritize a possible airway threat after neck surgery.

questions.stem: A 30-bed medical unit has an RN, an LPN and an assistive personnel (AP) caring for a group of clients whose conditions are stable. For each task, select every team member who may perform it for a stable client.

rows.text: Measuring and recording intake and output
Giving a scheduled subcutaneous insulin dose
Developing the client's plan of care
Reinforcing teaching about a low-sodium diet that the RN already gave

rationale.correct: Know each role's scope: AP do routine tasks such as intake and output, LPNs add medications and reinforcement of teaching, and only the RN plans care.

perOption.r1:c3: Recording intake and output is within AP training.
perOption.r2:c2: Giving medications to stable clients is within LPN scope.
perOption.r2:c3: AP do not give medications in acute care.
perOption.r3:c1: Care planning is an RN responsibility.
perOption.r3:c2: LPNs contribute data but do not develop the plan.
perOption.r4:c2: LPNs may reinforce teaching the RN has given.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Identify who may perform each task.

questions.stem: The RN is planning care with an assistive personnel (AP) on a busy medical unit. Which 3 tasks are appropriate to delegate to the AP?

options.text: Helping a stable client who had a stroke last month with a bed bath
Taking vital signs every 4 hours on a client with stable pneumonia
Checking the skin of a client admitted an hour ago for any pressure injuries
Ambulating a client 3 days after a hip replacement who walked with the physical therapist today
Watching a client during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion
Teaching a client after surgery how to use an incentive spirometer correctly

rationale.correct: Delegate routine, predictable tasks for stable clients; keep assessment, monitoring of high-risk therapies and teaching.

perOption.a: Routine hygiene for a stable client is within AP training.
perOption.b: Routine vital signs on a stable client can be delegated, with abnormal values reported.
perOption.c: Assessment of a new admission is an RN responsibility.
perOption.d: Walking a client whose response is known is within AP scope.
perOption.e: Monitoring for transfusion reactions needs RN assessment.
perOption.f: Teaching cannot be delegated to AP.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Choose tasks to delegate to AP.

questions.stem: A nurse is reviewing the five rights of delegation with a new graduate. Complete the sentence.

content.template: Before delegating to an AP, the nurse confirms the task is the right task for {{b1}}, gives clear {{b2}}, and after the task is done, the nurse remains responsible for {{b3}}.

options.text: a stable client with a predictable outcome
any client who is too busy for the nurse
a client who has just been admitted
directions, including what to report and when
permission to change the plan if needed
a checklist and then leave the AP alone
supervising and evaluating the outcome
nothing further, since the AP is now accountable
only documenting that the task was delegated

rationale.correct: Five rights: right task, right circumstance, right person, right directions and communication, right supervision and evaluation.

perOption.b1:a: Delegation suits stable clients whose response is predictable.
perOption.b1:b: Workload is not a reason to delegate care that needs judgment.
perOption.b2:a: Clear communication includes the expected result and what to report.
perOption.b2:b: AP cannot change the plan of care.
perOption.b3:a: Accountability for the outcome stays with the RN.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: During a counseling session, a client says, "When I get out, I'm going to kill my ex-partner. I know where they work." The client has a history of violence. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Keep the statement confidential, since the client shared it in a private session
Report the threat to the team so the duty to warn can be carried out
Ask the client to promise not to act on the threat and write the promise in the record
Call the ex-partner on the nurse's own phone to warn them right away

rationale.correct: A specific threat to an identifiable person creates a duty to warn and protect (Tarasoff); report it to the team and follow facility and legal procedures.

perOption.a: Confidentiality does not cover a serious, specific threat to an identifiable person.
perOption.b: A specific threat against an identifiable person creates a duty to warn and protect; the team follows the legal process.
perOption.c: A promise does not protect the ex-partner.
perOption.d: The warning is carried out through the team and legal process, not personally.

questions.stem: Which situations make a client's consent for surgery invalid? Select all that apply.

options.text: The client signed 30 minutes after receiving IV morphine and is drowsy
The surgeon explained the risks and alternatives, and the client asked several thoughtful questions
The client's child pressured the client to sign by threatening to stop visiting
The form was explained in English, which the client does not read or speak well, without an interpreter
The client signed and then the procedure was changed to a different operation
The client is 82 years old, lives alone and uses a walker at home

rationale.correct: Valid consent needs capacity, understanding, voluntariness and agreement to the specific procedure explained.

perOption.e: Consent covers only the procedure explained.
perOption.f: Age and living situation do not affect capacity.

questions.stem: For each situation, choose the document that applies.

cells.text: A client wants to name a sister to make health decisions if the client cannot
A client with advanced heart failure wants portable medical orders that travel between settings
A client writes that they do not want tube feeding if permanently unconscious

options.text: Durable power of attorney for health care
Living will
Do-not-resuscitate order
Living will
POLST form
Durable power of attorney for health care
Living will
POLST form
Do-not-resuscitate order

rationale.correct: A health care power of attorney names an agent; a living will records wishes; POLST and DNR are provider orders.

perOption.b1:a: It appoints a health care agent.
perOption.b1:b: A living will lists wishes but does not name an agent.
perOption.b1:c: A DNR is a provider order about CPR.
perOption.b2:a: A living will is not a medical order.
perOption.b2:b: POLST is a portable medical order for seriously ill clients.
perOption.b2:c: This names an agent, not orders.
perOption.b3:a: A living will records treatment wishes.
perOption.b3:b: POLST is completed with a provider as orders.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.stem: A unit uses the Plan-Do-Study-Act model to reduce delays in giving first antibiotic doses. Place the steps in order.

items.text: Do: try the change on a small scale for 2 weeks
Act: adopt, adapt or abandon the change
Plan a change, such as stocking first doses in the unit cabinet
Study the data on time to first dose before and after

rationale.correct: PDSA: plan, do (small test), study (analyze results), act (adopt, adapt or abandon).

perOption.a: Plan the change and predict its effect.
perOption.b: Test it on a small scale.
perOption.d: Decide what to do based on results.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The charge nurse makes notes during the night shift. Highlight the findings that are a risk to client safety and need action.

segments.text: RN in room 10 has worked 16 hours straight after covering a call-out
A float nurse was assigned a client on a titrated insulin drip without orientation to the protocol
The crash cart check was completed and signed
Two nurses are sharing one working glucose meter for the whole unit

rationale.correct: Address staff fatigue, unsafe assignments and equipment shortages promptly, since they increase the risk of errors.

perOption.s2: Fatigue after very long shifts increases errors.
perOption.s6: Unfamiliar high-alert therapy is a safety risk.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize system risks to client safety.

questions.stem: The case manager is identifying clients at highest risk of readmission within 30 days. Which client is at greatest risk?

options.text: A 45-year-old after an uncomplicated appendectomy who lives with a spouse and has insurance
A 79-year-old with heart failure, eight medicines, a recent admission and no help at home
A 30-year-old with a sprained ankle who has crutches and a follow-up visit booked
A 60-year-old after a knee replacement who is going to an inpatient rehabilitation facility for therapy

rationale.correct: Readmission risk rises with older age, heart failure or COPD, polypharmacy, recent admissions, low health literacy and poor social support.

perOption.b: Older age, heart failure, polypharmacy, a recent admission and lack of support all raise readmission risk.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Identify clients at high risk of readmission.

questions.stem: The discharge planning nurse reviews four clients who are going home this week. For each client need, indicate the most appropriate referral.

rows.text: Trouble swallowing thin liquids after a stroke
Needs a walker and gait training after hip surgery
Cannot afford medications and has no transportation
Needs adaptive utensils to eat after a hand injury

rationale.correct: PT: mobility and gait. OT: daily activities and adaptive equipment. SLP: speech and swallowing. Social work: financial, housing and transport.

perOption.r2:c1: PT provides gait training and walkers.
perOption.r3:c4: Social workers find financial and transport resources.
perOption.r4:c2: OT provides adaptive equipment for daily activities.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client's blood pressure has dropped to 84/50 mm Hg and the nurse believes the client is bleeding. The provider says by phone, "Just recheck it in an hour." Which statement by the nurse best uses structured communication to raise the concern?

options.text: "Okay, I'll recheck it in an hour and call you back with the reading."
"I'm concerned and uncomfortable. This is a safety issue; please come now."
"The other provider on call last night would have come to see the client by now."
"Fine. I'll document that you refused to come and see the client."

rationale.correct: Use structured tools such as CUS or two-challenge rule to escalate safety concerns, then the chain of command if not resolved.

perOption.a: This accepts a plan the nurse believes is unsafe.
perOption.b: The CUS approach (concerned, uncomfortable, safety issue) clearly escalates a safety concern.
perOption.c: Comparing providers does not state the concern clearly.
perOption.d: This is confrontational and does not get the client seen.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Escalate a safety concern using structured communication.

questions.stem: The nurse is planning discharge for a client with COPD. For each concern, select the appropriate actions.

groups.label: Concern: the client has fallen twice at home

options.text: Refer for a home safety evaluation
Advise the client to stay in bed most of the day
Arrange physical therapy for strength and balance

groups.label: Concern: the client cannot afford inhalers

options.text: Connect the client with a social worker or pharmacy assistance program
Tell the client to use the inhaler only when very short of breath
Ask the provider whether a lower-cost equivalent is available

rationale.correct: Discharge planning addresses each barrier: home safety and strength for falls, and financial resources and cheaper equivalents for medication costs.

perOption.b: Bed rest increases weakness and falls.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A competent client asks that no information about their condition be given to their adult son, who calls every day. The son calls and demands an update. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Give the son a brief update, since family has a right to know
Say that the nurse cannot share information and suggest asking the client
Ask the son for his reasons and share information if they seem good
Put the call through to the provider so the provider can decide what to say to the son

rationale.correct: Competent clients decide who may receive their health information; respect their choice even with close family.

perOption.a: The client's wishes about sharing information must be respected.
perOption.b: The nurse honors the client's privacy choice without confirming details.
perOption.c: The client decides who receives information.
perOption.d: The provider is also bound by the client's wishes.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse copies the previous day's assessment into today's note in the electronic record and changes a few values. Why is this practice risky?

options.text: It takes longer than typing a whole new note from the beginning each day
It can carry forward findings that are no longer true for the client
It uses too much storage space in the electronic health record
It is not allowed under any facility policy in the country

rationale.correct: Copying forward documentation risks inaccurate records; document current findings for each assessment.

perOption.a: Speed is not the main concern.
perOption.b: Copy-and-paste can document outdated findings, leading to errors and legal risk.
perOption.c: Storage is not the main concern.
perOption.d: Policies vary; the main issue is accuracy.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is using the I-PASS format for a handoff. Which elements should be included? Select all that apply.

options.text: Illness severity, such as stable or watcher
A patient summary with key events and the plan
An action list of tasks with timing and owner
The nurse's opinion about the family's personalities
Situation awareness and contingency plans
Synthesis by the receiver, such as a read-back

rationale.correct: I-PASS: illness severity, patient summary, action list, situation awareness and contingency planning, synthesis by the receiver.

perOption.d: Opinions are not part of a structured handoff.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse who has worked 12-hour shifts on the last two days is asked to stay for a third 12-hour shift because of a call-out. The nurse feels exhausted and made a near-miss error earlier today. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Agree to stay, since refusing could be seen as abandoning clients
Tell the charge nurse that fatigue makes staying unsafe, and help find cover
Stay but take extra caffeine and skip breaks to stay alert
Leave the unit immediately without giving a handoff report to anyone

rationale.correct: Fatigue increases errors; nurses should decline extra shifts when unsafe, communicate clearly and hand off care properly.

perOption.a: Abandonment involves leaving clients after accepting them; declining a new shift while handing off safely is not abandonment.
perOption.b: Nurses have a duty to recognize when fatigue makes practice unsafe and to communicate it.
perOption.c: Caffeine does not reverse the risks of severe fatigue.
perOption.d: Leaving without a handoff is abandonment.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse believes a client with falling blood pressure is being harmed by a delay in care, and the concern has not been resolved after talking with the provider. Place the escalation steps in order.

items.text: Notify the nursing supervisor or house manager
Contact the medical director or chief of the service
Discuss the concern again with the provider using structured communication

rationale.correct: Chain of command: provider, charge nurse, nursing supervisor, then medical leadership.

perOption.a: Start at the point of care.
perOption.b: The next level of authority on the unit.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: During a home visit, a home health nurse finds an 88-year-old client in soiled bedding with no food in the house and untreated pressure injuries. The client's caregiver is a grandchild who lives with the client. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Talk with the grandchild and come back next week to see whether things have improved
Report suspected neglect to adult protective services as required by law
Clean the client and leave a grocery list for the grandchild
Ask the client whether they want the nurse to report anything

rationale.correct: Suspected elder abuse or neglect must be reported to adult protective services; provide immediate care and ensure safety.

perOption.a: Waiting leaves a vulnerable adult in danger.
perOption.b: Nurses are mandated reporters of suspected elder neglect.
perOption.c: Immediate care helps, but the neglect must also be reported.
perOption.d: Reporting suspected neglect does not depend on the client's request.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A family of four is brought to the emergency department in January after running a gas generator in the attached garage during a power outage. The parent has a headache, nausea and confusion, and their SpO2 reads 98% on room air. The children are drowsy. Complete the diagram by placing the condition the parent is most likely experiencing, 2 actions the nurse should take, and 2 parameters the nurse should monitor.

actions.text: Rely on the SpO2 reading to judge the oxygen level
Give 2 L/min of oxygen by nasal cannula
Send the family home once the headache improves

parameters.text: Level of consciousness and neurological status
Bowel sounds in each of the four quadrants
Body weight measured once a week

rationale.correct: CO poisoning: 100% oxygen, carboxyhemoglobin level, neurological monitoring and possible hyperbaric therapy; pulse oximetry is falsely normal.

perOption.c1: Headache, nausea and confusion in several family members exposed to a generator indoors point to CO poisoning; pulse oximetry falsely reads normal.
perOption.c2: Gastroenteritis does not cause confusion in a whole family after a generator exposure.
perOption.c3: A whole family would not develop migraines together.
perOption.c4: The exposure and neurological signs point to CO.
perOption.a1: High-flow oxygen speeds removal of carbon monoxide.
perOption.a2: This confirms CO poisoning; pulse oximetry cannot detect it.
perOption.a3: Pulse oximetry reads carboxyhemoglobin as oxygenated hemoglobin.
perOption.p2: Shows brain effects and need for hyperbaric therapy.
perOption.p3: Not a guide to CO poisoning.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize and treat carbon monoxide poisoning.

questions.stem: Only shared rooms are available. For each pair of clients, indicate whether they can share a room.

rows.text: Two clients who both have confirmed MRSA wound infections and no other infections
A client with influenza and a client after a hip replacement
A client receiving chemotherapy with neutropenia and a client with a urinary tract infection
Two clients after uncomplicated elective knee surgery

rationale.correct: Cohort clients with the same organism; keep infected clients away from immunocompromised and surgical clients.

perOption.r1:c1: Cohorting clients with the same organism is acceptable.
perOption.r1:c2: They have the same organism, so they can share.
perOption.r2:c1: The influenza could spread to the surgical client.
perOption.r2:c2: Influenza needs droplet precautions away from uninfected clients.
perOption.r3:c1: A neutropenic client should not share with an infected client.
perOption.r4:c1: No infection risk to each other.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Before the incision in a laparoscopic appendectomy, the nurse reviews the surgical safety checklist. Highlight the items that are not completed and must be resolved before surgery begins.

cells: Client identity confirmed with two identifiers
Antibiotic given within 60 minutes before incision

rationale.correct: The surgical safety checklist includes identity, site marking, allergies, antibiotic timing and a team time-out before incision.

perOption.r2: The site must be marked by the surgeon before surgery.
perOption.r3: Prophylactic antibiotic timing must be confirmed.
perOption.r5: The time-out must happen right before incision.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: While checking a newly admitted client's belongings on a psychiatric unit, the nurse finds a folding knife in a jacket pocket. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Return the jacket and ask the client to keep the knife out of sight
Secure the knife per policy and notify security and the charge nurse
Ask the client why they have the knife before deciding what to do
Throw the knife into the regular trash can in the client's room right away

rationale.correct: Weapons found in belongings are secured per policy, with security and the charge nurse notified and documentation completed.

perOption.a: Weapons cannot remain on the unit.
perOption.b: Weapons are removed and secured per policy to protect clients and staff.
perOption.c: The knife is removed first; the conversation can follow.
perOption.d: The weapon must be secured and documented, not left accessible.

references: Psychiatric-mental health nursing texts (e.g. Varcarolis; Halter)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: Which practices help prevent medication errors in children? Select all that apply.

options.text: Recording weight in kilograms only
Using oral syringes for liquid medicines
Using household teaspoons to measure doses at home
Having a second nurse independently double-check high-alert drugs
Calculating the dose and checking it against the safe dose range
Rounding all doses up to the nearest whole milliliter

rationale.correct: Pediatric medication safety: weights in kilograms, safe dose range checks, oral syringes, independent double checks and accurate measuring devices.

perOption.a: Mixing pounds and kilograms causes dosing errors.
perOption.b: Oral syringes prevent IV administration of oral liquids and measure accurately.
perOption.e: Checking the safe range catches errors.
perOption.f: Rounding can cause significant errors in small children.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

questions.stem: A 7-year-old with spina bifida is scheduled for surgery. Which precaution is most important for the perioperative team to plan?

options.text: Schedule the child as the last case of the day to allow more time
Use a latex-free environment and latex-free equipment throughout
Avoid giving antibiotics during surgery to prevent allergic reactions
Use extra adhesive tape to secure the IV because the child may move

rationale.correct: Children with spina bifida are at high risk of latex allergy; provide a latex-free environment from birth onward.

perOption.a: Latex-safe scheduling usually means the first case, when airborne latex is lowest.
perOption.b: Children with spina bifida have a high risk of latex allergy because of repeated early exposure.
perOption.c: Prophylactic antibiotics are still given as indicated.
perOption.d: Tape is not the main concern.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)
Written to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
